name: v0.3.6
body:
AnswerLens is a CLI-first AI visibility auditor for product websites.

CI for AI discoverability.

## Start here

- Open the live demo report: https://yscjrh.github.io/ai-visibility-auditor/examples/static-good/index.html
- Run the 60-second fixture demo: https://github.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor#run-the-60-second-fixture-demo
- Run a 5-minute real-site audit: https://github.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md
- Add the GitHub Action: https://github.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/blob/main/docs/github-action.md
- Download assets from this release: CLI tarball, demo audit bundle, and compiled site bundle

## Release asset checklist

- CLI tarball: use the versioned `answerlens-cli-*.tgz` package for pinned local CLI runs before npm is visible
- `answerlens-demo-audit.tar.gz`: unpack the fixture report and open `share-summary.md`, then `scorecard.md`, then `recommendations.md`
- The Release Distribution workflow runs `pnpm release:assets:smoke -- --dir dist --work-dir dist/release-assets-smoke-check --summary-out dist/release-assets-smoke-summary.md` before uploading release assets
- `release-assets-smoke-summary.md` is kept in the workflow summary and internal artifact as maintainer review evidence; do not treat it as standalone adoption proof
- `Release review path`: open `release-assets-summary.md`, then the demo audit `share-summary.md`, then `scorecard.md`, then `recommendations.md`
- `answerlens-site.tar.gz`: inspect the compiled Pages bundle for docs, examples, starter, and release pages at this tag
- `release-assets-manifest.json`: verify asset sizes and SHA-256 checksums before reusing downloaded release assets
- `release-assets-summary.md`: read the verified asset table and adopter handoff before forwarding or reusing downloaded release assets
- If `npm view @answerlens/cli` returns `404`, keep release assets or local checkout as the public path; do not present npm as activated

## What ships

- Release assets rebuilt from the current `main` state after the release smoke-summary evidence pass
- Release asset smoke summaries in the workflow summary and internal release-distribution artifact
- Release snapshot checking that supports planned release PRs while still verifying the latest published release
- Starter bundle and GitHub Action docs pinned to the reviewed `v0.3.6` Action release
- The same fixture demo, consumer-repo demo, public-claim checks, typecheck, tests, and SEO checks as the release gate
- Publish-ready CLI bundle and tarball plus repo-native report artifacts

## Known limits

- No consumer AI UI scraping
- No ranking guarantees
- No promise of answer placement in ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overview, or any answer surface
- Readiness and VAVR are diagnostic signals, not platform rankings
- Optional `eval` is BYOK; secrets stay in environment variables or GitHub secrets, not `runtime.yaml`
- Public summaries and default GitHub artifacts should not expose raw provider payloads
- The Codex plugin is a maintainer workflow helper, not a new audit engine or public SaaS surface
- GitHub Pages deployment still depends on repository settings
- npm publish is skipped unless NPM_TOKEN or trusted publishing is configured

## Canonical docs

- README: https://github.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor#readme
- Chinese README: https://github.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md
- GitHub-native growth plan: https://github.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/blob/main/docs/github-growth-plan.md
- Distribution plan: https://github.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/blob/main/docs/distribution-plan.md
- Manual steps: https://github.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/blob/main/docs/manual-steps.md
- Quickstart: https://github.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md

- Trust and safety: https://github.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/blob/main/docs/trust-and-safety.md
- First-run story: https://github.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/blob/main/docs/first-run-story.md
- Codex plugin: https://github.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/blob/main/docs/codex-plugin.md

name: v0.2.0
body:
## What ships

AnswerLens `v0.2.0` is a CLI-first, report-driven AI visibility auditor for product websites.

This release ships:

- `audit` for deterministic AI-readiness checks against live sites or local fixtures
- `eval` for prompt-pack benchmarking with OpenAI and Perplexity adapters
- `manual-import` for scoring normalized external or human-collected answer samples
- machine-readable and shareable outputs including `run.json`, `scorecard.md`, `recommendations.md`, `index.html`, `eval-summary.json`, and citation gap matrices
- a launch-ready README surface with a repo-local cover, scorecard preview, artifact preview, and before/after showcase

## What changed in PR #8

Launch hardening landed in [PR #8](https://github.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/pull/8) and moved AnswerLens from "credible local MVP" to "publicly presentable open-source release":

- protected the private blueprint by ignoring `seofull.md`
- fixed the HTML scorecard separator mojibake regression
- corrected `manual-import` run metadata so `run.mode` and `run.json.kind` stay honest
- expanded the prompt pack to 35 prompts with 10 holdouts
- added regression tests for README assets, manual-import manifests, holdout counts, and scorecard HTML output
- aligned README, docs, workflow summaries, and labels with the current public contract

## Cover

![AnswerLens cover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/v0.2.0/assets/readme-cover.svg)

## Sample outputs

![AnswerLens scorecard preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/v0.2.0/assets/readme-scorecard-preview.svg)

![AnswerLens artifact preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/v0.2.0/assets/readme-artifacts-preview.svg)

## Public roadmap

The canonical public roadmap now lives at [docs/roadmap.md](https://github.com/YSCJRH/ai-visibility-auditor/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md). PR #15 fixed `AnswerLens` as the primary public brand and set the execution path as `#9 -> #10 -> (#11 + #12) -> (#13 + #14)`.

## Known limits

- AnswerLens does not scrape consumer AI UIs.
- AnswerLens does not guarantee placement or ranking on any answer surface.
- Search Console, Bing Webmaster, and IndexNow remain follow-up milestone work rather than part of this release.
- The current Figma seat is view-only, so the shipped visuals are repository SVG assets rather than synced Figma source files.

## Next milestones

- `v0.1-audit`: schema-text consistency, evidence density, internal link context, and rule registry hardening
- `v0.2-eval`: manual rank import and CPS scoring, plus multi-sample stability summaries
- `v0.3-connectors`: Search Console, Bing Webmaster, and IndexNow validation helpers

name: v0.1.0-alpha.1
body:
Initial public alpha for AnswerLens.

What is supported now:
- CLI-first AI-readiness audit for product sites and fixtures
- OpenAI-backed experimental eval with normalized citations and raw payload persistence
- Markdown, JSON, and static HTML reports
- Brief generation for FAQ, compare, and use-case gaps

What this is not:
- Not a rank tracker for consumer AI UIs
- Not a generic AI content generator
- Not a replacement for Search Console or analytics
